title: Real-Life Graphs
seo_title: Year 9 Real-Life Graphs Worksheets: Conversion Graphs, Distance-Time Graphs and Cost Graphs
standard_text: Reduce a given linear equation in two variables to the standard form y = mx + c; calculate and interpret gradients and intercepts of graphs of such linear equations numerically, graphically and algebraically; find approximate solutions to contextual problems from given graphs of a variety of functions, including piece-wise linear graphs.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 real-life graphs worksheets: read conversion graphs, distance-time graphs (stops and speed), cost graphs with a fixed charge, and filling containers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: On a distance-time graph, the gradient is the speed.
key_sub: Flat line: stopped. Steeper line: faster.
body_html:
How it works

Real-life graphs show how one quantity changes with another. On a conversion graph, go up from one axis to the line, then across to the other axis.

On a distance-time graph, a flat line means stopped, a steeper line means faster, and the gradient is the speed. On a cost graph, where the line meets the vertical axis is the fixed charge and the gradient is the cost per unit.

Example

A line goes up 20 km in 30 minutes.

30 minutes = 0.5 h.

20 ÷ 0.5.

Answer: 40 km/h

Example

A taxi graph starts at £3 and rises £2 per mile.

Fixed charge £3, rate £2 per mile.

Answer: Cost for 5 miles: £13

Example

A flat section from 10:00 to 10:45.

Distance does not change.

Answer: Stopped for 45 minutes

Common mistakes

  • Reading the wrong axis.
  • Thinking a flat line on a distance-time graph means moving at a steady speed.
  • Working out speed as time ÷ distance, or forgetting to change minutes into hours.
  • Taking the fixed charge as the cost per unit.

faq.q: How do I read a conversion graph?
faq.a: Find the value on one axis, go to the line, then across or down to the other axis.

faq.q: How do I find speed from a distance-time graph?
faq.a: Speed = distance ÷ time for that section, which is the gradient of the line. Change minutes into hours for km/h.

faq.q: What does a horizontal line mean on a distance-time graph?
faq.a: The distance is not changing, so the person or vehicle has stopped.

faq.q: What is the fixed charge on a cost graph?
faq.a: The cost when nothing has been used: where the line crosses the vertical axis.

items.e: Speed = distance ÷ time = 3 km ÷ 0.75 h = 4 km/h.

items.q: On a distance-time graph, what does a horizontal (flat) line show?
items.e: Distance does not change, so the person is not moving.

items.q: On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line show?
items.e: More distance in the same time means a faster speed.

items.q: On a distance-time graph (distance from home), what does a line sloping down show?
items.e: The distance from home is getting smaller: travelling back towards home.

items.q: What does the gradient of a distance-time graph represent?
items.e: Gradient = distance ÷ time = speed.

items.q: A distance-time graph goes up 30 km in 2 hours. What is the speed?
A distance-time graph goes up 12 km in 30 minutes. What is the speed?
items.e: 30 minutes = 0.5 hours. 12 ÷ 0.5 = 24 km/h.

items.q: A cyclist rides 20 km in 1 hour, stops for 30 minutes, then rides 10 km in 30 minutes. Which part is fastest?
c: Both riding parts are the same speed
items.e: First: 20 km/h. Last: 10 ÷ 0.5 = 20 km/h. Both riding parts are the same speed.

items.q: Why can a distance-time graph never go straight up (vertical)?
c: It can, if you are fast
Because the axes are the wrong way round
That would mean moving a distance in no time
items.e: A vertical line means distance changes with zero time passing: moving a distance in no time, which is impossible.

items.q: Two walkers' graphs cross. What does the crossing point show?
c: They are at the same place at the same time
items.e: Same distance and same time: they are at the same place at the same time.

items.q: A graph of a car's journey is a curve that gets steeper. What is the car doing?
items.e: The gradient (speed) is increasing: speeding up.

items.q: A distance-time graph is a straight line from (0, 0) to (3 hours, 150 km). What is the average speed?
A train travels at a steady 80 km/h. Which graph shape shows this on a distance-time graph?
items.e: Steady speed is a constant gradient: a straight line sloping upwards.

items.q: On a speed-time graph, what does a horizontal line show?
items.e: On a speed-time graph the height is the speed, so a flat line means a constant speed. (On a distance-time graph it would mean stopped.)

items.q: Water is poured at a steady rate into a cylinder. What does the graph of depth against time look like?
items.e: A cylinder has the same width all the way up, so the depth rises steadily: a straight line.

items.q: Water is poured at a steady rate into a cone standing on its point. What does the graph of depth against time look like?
c: A curve that gets less steep
items.e: The cone gets wider higher up, so the depth rises more slowly: a curve that gets less steep.

items.q: Water is poured at a steady rate into a bowl that is narrow at the top. What happens to the depth graph near the top?
items.e: A narrower part fills up faster, so it gets steeper.

items.q: A plumber charges £40 call-out plus £30 per hour. Where does the cost graph cross the cost axis?
items.e: At 0 hours you still pay the call-out fee: £40.

items.q: A cost graph is a straight line from (0, £5) to (10 km, £25). What is the cost per km?
Which of these graphs would go through the origin?
c: Plumber's bill with a call-out charge
Phone bill with a monthly fee
items.e: 0 pounds is 0 euros, so pounds against euros goes through (0, 0). The others have a fixed charge.

items.q: A temperature graph rises from 8 am to 2 pm, then falls. When was it warmest?
items.e: The highest point is at 2 pm.
